minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to pursue a 53 E-and-a-half revolving account and set beach season dates, May 5 to Sept 15.
minutes.summary: The Commission approved three sets of minutes, adopted a no hunting, trapping or firearms policy for park properties, and voted to pursue switching the parks revolving account to a type that needs Town Meeting approval. It set seasonal beach employment dates, began discussing beach fees, passes and a rental policy (tabled to next meeting), and discussed the skate park group's location decision, Marshall Park planning, a volunteer day and a maintenance reporting policy.

votes.motion: Approve the January 11 minutes as amended
Approve the wording of the no hunting, trapping or discharge of firearms policy for park properties
Pursue the 53 E and a half revolving account as the new destination, and authorize drafting a warrant article
Send the seasonal employment application to the state for May 5 through September 15

budget_items.what_was_said: Balance over the limit at year end is supposed to close to the general fund, which has not been done. Members worry fees meant for maintenance could be swept away.

budget_items.topic: Alternative 53 E and a half revolving account
budget_items.what_was_said: Allows carrying over a balance but requires a bylaw change and an annual Town Meeting spending limit. It could also pay program staff from program fees.

budget_items.topic: Beach season passes and daily fees
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff proposed bringing back season passes and keeping the daily rates. Revenue did not come close to covering beach payroll last year.
A member asked what share of payroll fees should cover and suggested free access if recovery is low. Staff said last year was not representative and more data is needed.
Proposed hourly rates for the beach house and grounds with a refundable deposit. Members questioned whether the deposit covers damage or overtime.
Hires who complete the course will be reimbursed for their certification cost.

budget_items.topic: Capital plan funding for Marshall Park planning
budget_items.what_was_said: Marshall Park planning is next on the capital project list if more money becomes available.

budget_items.topic: Parks maintenance costs held in facilities budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director believes much of park grounds maintenance is paid from facilities, not the parks line. Members want to see numbers and possibly move them to the parks line.
The rink order was delayed and not paid for; staff plans to order one later, possibly for Wallace.

decisions.decision: December 14 minutes held for correction; January 11 minutes amended the same night.
Chair will tell the skate park group to watch the video and come back when ready to say whether they want Marshall Park; Commission will treat them as not coming if they do not answer.
Chair and Dave to work with the Town Manager, Town Accountant and DPW director on drafting the warrant article, aiming for the May town meeting.
Beach policy, fees and rental policy tabled to the next meeting; documents should be sent a day ahead.
Marshall Park list review deferred to next meeting with a time limit; members to send lists to Kayla to compile.
Chris to co-coordinate a volunteer cleanup around Earth Day with Kayla.
Maintenance policy: Kayla to tweak the reporting form, and Chair to draft wording for a walk-through policy for the next meeting.
Next meeting set for March 1 at 6:30 p.m.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to pursue a different type of parks revolving account and to authorize a warrant article for Town Meeting.
The Commission voted to send the state a seasonal beach employment application covering May 5 through September 15.
The Commission approved the wording of a policy banning hunting, trapping and the discharge of firearms on park properties.
Beach fees, season passes and a beach rental policy were discussed, and the policy, fees and rental policy were tabled to the next meeting.
The skate park group was asked to say whether it wants Marshall Park, and Marshall Park list review was deferred to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The current parks revolving account is supposed to close any balance over its limit to the general fund at year end, so fees collected for park maintenance could be swept away; the proposed account type would let a balance carry over, but needs a Town Meeting vote and an annual spending limit.

Beach fees and passes are not set yet, and members said last year's revenue did not come close to covering beach payroll, so what residents pay to use the beach and how much the town budget, mostly taxes, covers is still open.
Members said much park grounds maintenance may be paid from the facilities budget rather than the parks line, so the parks line may not show what parks cost.
watch_next: Next meeting, March 1 at 6:30 p.m.: beach policy, fees and rental policy, and the Marshall Park list review.
The warrant article for the parks revolving account, which the Chair and Dave are drafting with town officials, aimed at the May town meeting.
